answer: On a 12-item scored numeric set, honest anonymous Delphi (median feedback, evidence-retaining revision) tightened mean relative IQR 0.2500 -> 0.1125 while mean relative individual MAE 0.1443 -> 0.0673 (raw mean IQR 3133002.922802594 -> 1409851.3152611682; raw mean MAE 1808190.258303211 -> 843225.3580800127). All 12 items classified CONVERGENCE and the runtime allowed a confident consensus. Seeding one stubborn confident-wrong seat and switching to attributed high-confidence feedback reversed the accuracy trajectory: mean relative MAE 0.4786 -> 2.3365 while relative IQR 0.2500 -> 0.0250. All 12 items classified HERDING; maybe_report_consensus withheld confident_consensus (withheld_reason=herding). A dispersion-only claim on the same raw IQRs would have called CONVERGENCE on every herding item. The same plant under anonymous median feedback did not herd (herding_items=0); attributed minus anonymous final relative MAE = 1.9169. Falling dispersion is therefore not treated as convergence.

question: Delphi is listed as a topology at :10926, and its whole premise is that iterated anonymous feedback improves estimates. Measure across rounds both the dispersion of estimates and the accuracy against ground truth on a scored question set. Falling dispersion with flat or worsening accuracy is herding, not convergence, and the runtime must be able to tell the difference before it reports a confident consensus.
